project_sections.heading: A storefront for one-of-one pieces
project_sections.body: Off The Rack is a digital storefront for one-of-one and upcycled fashion. The experience brings product browsing, product categories, and availability into a responsive website.

project_sections.heading: From browsing to the details
project_sections.body: The storefront connects product listings and product detail views with a custom inquiry flow. Responsive interfaces carry the experience across screen sizes.

project_sections.heading: The work behind the storefront
project_sections.body: Next.js and TypeScript support the frontend. Supabase powers product administration and database integration, with Vercel used for deployment. My role covered UI/UX design, frontend development, and the database/admin connection.

project_sections.heading: Design meets a working product
project_sections.body: This project brings interface design, frontend development, and product administration into one responsive storefront. The screenshots and initial wireframe show the interface and the system behind it.

project_sections.heading: An independent point of view
project_sections.body: This is an independent redesign concept for Marci Metzger Homes, not an official client engagement. The project reworks a real-estate homepage as a clearer editorial experience.

project_sections.heading: Give the content room to breathe
project_sections.body: The redesign uses an editorial visual system within a responsive single-page homepage. The original provided copy and source photography are preserved.

project_sections.heading: Built for the browser
project_sections.body: The frontend uses HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Node/npm, Playwright, and Vercel in the project toolset. The experience includes accessible interactions and a responsive layout.

project_sections.heading: A clearer editorial experience
project_sections.body: The concept explores how layout, typography, and responsive behavior can reshape a real-estate homepage while retaining its provided content and photography.

project_sections.heading: Monitoring at a glance
project_sections.body: The desktop dashboard groups system information, a deployment archive, and connection status. The analytics screen presents mission information and hardware diagnostics as separate areas.

project_sections.heading: Camera and telemetry together
project_sections.body: The drone-stream screen places a camera view between system-status information and battery, detection, and payload panels. Gauges and status labels provide another way to read the displayed telemetry.

project_sections.heading: A mobile view of the same system
project_sections.body: The supplied mobile dashboard uses system-summary cards, a recent-flight list, and bottom navigation for home, analytics, and logs.

project_sections.heading: A game world across screens
project_sections.body: The home screen combines the selected character, equipment, current quest, and daily quest information. Pixel-art characters and a forest setting carry through the supplied game UI designs.

project_sections.heading: Heroes, gear, and battle
project_sections.body: The hero screen pairs a selection grid with character details. The equipment screen connects an inventory grid to item information, while the battle screen shows opposing characters, health bars, a timer, and touch controls.

project_sections.heading: An introduction to everyday planning
project_sections.body: Three welcome screens introduce Task Mate through task illustrations, short planning messages, and a final choice between login and sign-up. A dark background and blue accents establish the visual direction.

project_sections.heading: A clear path into an account
project_sections.body: Login and registration share a rounded white form panel over the dark background. Account fields, a sign-up and login switch, password recovery, and alternate sign-in options keep the entry screens visually connected.

project_sections.heading: Daily tasks and a calendar view
project_sections.body: The home screen brings a completion summary, category filters, and timed task cards into one view. The calendar pairs a month grid with the selected day's schedule. Both screens share bottom navigation and a prominent central add button.

project_sections.heading: Two ways to read the day
Progress and personal preferences
project_sections.body: Statistics show completion rate, task totals, a streak, weekly activity, and progress by category. The profile groups task summaries with account, notification, appearance, and privacy settings.

project_sections.heading: Account and communication paths
project_sections.body: Separate flows describe login, sign-up, password recovery, study-together views, and chat. Decision branches show validation, error paths, and the return to the main view.

project_sections.heading: Finding a study partner
project_sections.body: The main-view diagram maps location permission, user cards, match decisions, and the study-together view. A separate navigation flow links home, study together, chat, and profile destinations.

project_sections.heading: Delivery and retrieval
project_sections.body: The diagram separates delivery from retrieval. Delivery uses an OTP verification path; retrieval uses an RFID verification path. Each flow includes assigned-locker checks and door or package conditions.

project_sections.heading: The resident's path
project_sections.body: The user-side flow starts at the DropSafe dashboard, then moves through login, locker status, OTP generation, delivery notification, and retrieval. The system flow documents the connected status and event updates.

project_sections.heading: A map of the messaging system
project_sections.body: The use-case diagram separates customer and administrator responsibilities. It covers account access, senders, recipient lists, individual messages, campaigns, tracking, and administration.

project_sections.heading: Actions and decisions
project_sections.body: User/system swimlanes separate user actions from system responses. The supplied flows document sender verification, message composition, and campaign scheduling, including validation and return paths.
